t: The Sasanian Empire ruled Iran and Mesopotamia from 224 to 651, a centralised Zoroastrian monarchy that was Rome's great rival for four centuries.
Its armoured cavalry, fixed land tax and court culture shaped Byzantium and, above all, the Islamic caliphates that followed.
A ruinous war with Byzantium and a succession crisis left it defenceless against the Arab conquests that ended it by 651.
dyk: Shapur I captured the Roman emperor Valerian at Edessa in 260, the only time a reigning Roman emperor was taken prisoner by a foreign power.
ev: Ardashir I defeats and kills the last Parthian king, Artabanus IV, at Hormozdgan
Shapur I captures the Roman emperor Valerian at the Battle of Edessa
Shapur II wins Nisibis and lands beyond the Tigris in a peace with Rome's Jovian
Khosrow I and the Göktürks begin destroying the Hephthalite empire
Khosrow II's general Shahrbaraz captures Jerusalem
Heraclius defeats the Sasanians at the Battle of Nineveh
Arab armies destroy the main Sasanian field army at al-Qadisiyyah
The last king, Yazdegerd III, is murdered near Merv
